record_notes.DCP-LETT-1674: April 25, supplied 1855. Initiates alpine-range enquiry to Gray with a list copied from his Manual, asking memory-based habitat codes, intervening lowland distances and a comparative flora list. Enclosure is described but not fully transcribed here. Postmarks April 25, April 26 London and May 9 Boston describe carriage, not Gray reading date. Header handwriting uncertainty concerns Down/Farnborough, while Kent is Darwin hand; it does not displace main Darwin authorship. May 22 source explicitly answers this request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1695: June 8, supplied 1855. Explicitly answers Gray May 22, suggests geographic range codes and comparisons, explains exploratory rather than fixed questions, seeks close-species marks and queries inconsistent mountain distances. P3 compares family proportions then admits apparent agreement fails across other families. Crucially the preserved raw HTML itself contains flattened numerals 361798=149, 1092=19.2, 24206=18 and 2231798=18, with no MathML nodes: do not describe this as merely an extractor bug or silently reconstruct fractions/arithmetic. Hold reliable rendering of those numerical passages pending authoritative source verification. Later Gray publication is future; full scientific letter is an established response, with rendering hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1725: July 21, supplied 1855. Explicitly thanks for June 30 letter, close-species discussion and intended marking, while not knowing whether sheets arrived and suspecting they did not. Hooker has now read the Gray letter, unlike the earlier May letter merely forwarded. Hopes Gray writes species essay and distribution account; they are not complete. Postscript reports listed seeds germinated after eighty-two/eighty-five days, answering Gray interest. Entire four-block reply supported by 1707; physical marked-sheet receipt is not established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1749: August 24, supplied 1855. Responds to a different missing Gray letter received about a fortnight earlier, with note forwarded to Hooker and manuscript close-species list. This is not June 30 promised marked sheets. Gives 115 genera and 6.37 versus 4.67 species per genus, with Salix/Carex and single-species genera exclusions; claims qualified support and asks for possible fallacy. Uses Watson British marked flora as comparison, known by this date through 1743 shipment. Separate enquiry about variable organs cites Helianthemum and Pyrgoma; preserve report/example qualifications. Missing Dytiscus update and full manuscript list prevent direct training pair with 1707.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1407: Supplied April 21, 1851, Monday at Malvern. Short request that Fanny come after breakfast to feel Anne pulse, explicitly no change or hurry. No reply body or completed examination identified. Do not replace this immediate observation with later death knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1413: Supplied April 24, 1851 at Malvern, departure arrangements. Miss Martineau probably denotes a book, with two possible titles discussed in footnote; do not assert that Harriet personally travelled. Darwin expects to manage journey, asks about books, washing and Brodie, then cautions against Friday travel. Plans and historical instructions are not completed events or agent commands.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1417: Supplied April 25, 1851 at Down. Darwin P1–3 thanks Fanny for encouraging his return to Emma and undertaking Anne funeral, describes shared grief and requests grave location. P4 is explicitly in Emma hand, speaks of Charles in third person and must remain Emma voice, not Darwin grounding. Funeral sketch is cited by archive location but is not reproduced here. Same-day Fanny 1419 still awaits news of arrival and acknowledges a separate Emma note; it is not a demonstrated response to this newly written Darwin letter. April 28 source 1424 explicitly does answer the received gratitude.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1419: April 25, supplied 1851, Fanny at Malvern after nine-o-clock funeral. Addressed to both Emma and Charles despite catalogue naming Darwin alone. Describes funeral, grief of Brodie/Thorley, receipt of Emma note, intended Saturday departure and expected future news of Charles arrival. No evidence she read Darwin same-day Down letter 1417; geographic and content sequence instead distinguish the crossed communications. Fanny voice and later family memoir description are separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1424: April 28 with supplied month/year, Monday at Chester Terrace. Explicitly found letters from both Charles and Emma on returning Saturday, April 26, and echoes Darwin gratitude for her help enabling Thursday departure. Accept reverse response to 1417 P1–3 while noting separate missing Emma letter. Other paragraphs relay Elizabeth, Hannah, servants and family reactions, offer future help, promise accounts, and report Tollets written. Saturday receipt belongs to Fanny, not Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1547: August 18 with supplied month/year, 1854. Fanny missing illness note first informs Darwin about Erasmus fever, and he requests updates. His hope that improvement means worst over is an expectation, not confirmed recovery or medical fact. Retrospective thanks for comfort during Anne illness are not a response to an 1851 letter. Hooker August 25 comparison is later dating evidence only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1634: January 30, 1855 incoming Davy letter. Received missing Darwin enquiry this morning, offers future salmonid-ova experiments only when material available. P4 seventy-two-hour survival concerns a young charr barely covered with water, not ova exposed for seventy-two hours: editorial summary conflates these. P5 ova taken from trout stomach later hatched; P6 discusses moisture-preserved ova and only suspects partial drying fatal. Existing observations, proposed experiments and hypotheses remain distinct. Undated Darwin portfolio mark does not prove receipt January 30.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1651A: March 21, 1855 catalogue record with one bracketed editorial synopsis only. No authentic Davy letter or paper prose is transcribed. Record itself fully inspected, authentic body unavailable. Synopsis mentions January 28 enquiry, experimental conditions and intended Royal Society submission; it cannot be a training question. Subsequent Darwin acknowledgements identify a real paper, but do not supply its omitted wording. Differing 1856 publication references in nearby apparatus require version checking before any attempted recovery.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1653: March 25, supplied 1855. Arrived home late yesterday, March 24, and found Davy paper already there; its earlier physical delivery date is unstated. Pleased by epistolary form and plans to forward in two or three days. Has brought Angler and his Friend, but later April 25 reading record is not March completion. Documented reply to paper represented by synopsis-only 1651A, held as missing authentic prompt rather than fabricated Q/A.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1654: March 26, supplied 1855. Explicitly has just read Davy paper, reports interest in three-day moss exposure, moist-air survival, developmental-stage differences and temperature effects, requests possible replication and plans sending today. Do not infer that requested repetition happened; footnote finds no evidence. Royal Society March 27 receipt and April 26 reading are later external events. Bibliography lists a February 1856 reading under a differently described paper, requiring source-version care. Authentic incoming manuscript absent here, so no training pair with editorial synopsis.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1740: Additional full reading: Watson August 13, 1855, asks which kind of species to mark, contrasting Hooker and Jordan taxonomic scales. Complete separately placed Categories of Species enclosure read: four classes with Prunus, cherries, plum/sloe and bramble examples, distinctions explicitly grading into one another. Later joint Darwin/Watson wording changes quoted in footnotes and Darwin annotations are not automatically initial enclosure text/date. Marked British catalogue is not yet provided by this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1743: Additional full reading: Watson August 17, 1855 sends marked British catalogue and distinguishes selected close pairs from species/variety entries left unmarked; warns selection may not fit unknown purpose. Independently viewed stem diagram: straight left stalk and right stalk curved at base, illustrating Drosera distinction; no species labels or scale printed in image. Physical catalogue and separate pre-1847 publication list are not fully transcribed. Later October/November calculations and Natural selection counts in apparatus are not August body. Courtesy and phrenology comment remain Watson voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1747: Additional full reading: Watson August 23, 1855 responds to unlocated disclosure of Darwin numerical objective and Fries remark. Says prior marking was illustrative rather than numerically exact; British small genera can be globally large. Two textual diagrams compare equal extreme separation with denser intermediate species versus extreme separation scaling with species count; retain rows and many/few labels, not linear prose. Argues taxonomic grouping partly human and small-flora statistics weak indications. Future Saxifraga example postponed; Darwin marginal rebuttals are undated. This criticism does not itself demonstrate Darwin read it by August 24 merely because topics recur.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1685: Explicit prior primary reading reused from accepted batch-05 with source and note/ledger pins. Additional full reading of Gray May 22, 1855. Answers an unlocated-in-this-packet Darwin request and returns a completed habitat list, while offering fuller comparison and requesting methodological hints. North American flora plans remain prospective; last volumes were not in fact completed as expected. Alpine plant identities and Labrador occurrence include confidence levels and pending re-examination. Mountain distances in P7 were later corrected, not silently replaced in May text. Darwin marginal annotation below signature is cut off. No full enclosure transcription here. June 5 Hooker letter demonstrates Darwin reading this Gray letter and list; forwarding alone does not demonstrate Hooker read it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1707: Explicit prior primary reading reused from accepted batch-05 with source and note/ledger pins. Additional full reading of Gray June 30, 1855, explicitly answering June 8. Promises annotated Manual sheets with close species, discusses taxonomy and burden of evidence, plans newspaper reprinting and Morris fish-egg enquiry. Distinguish proposed sheets from later manuscript delivery and planned enquiry from already dispatched Morris June 17 letter described by editors. P12–14 correct earlier road-like distances to about seventy-five and sixty direct miles; retain correction chronology. Notes are undated. Bibliography includes unrelated George Robert Gray bird genera entry; do not confuse author identity with Asa Gray or treat that entry as letter voice.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Viewed preserved image: two drawn flowering stalks, the left long and straight, the right with conspicuously curved basal end. No printed labels or scale. Illustrates the straight versus curved-at-base diagnostic character discussed for Drosera; do not assign species labels solely from the unlabelled drawing.

reading_method: Fourteen target source records freshly read, one of them editorial synopsis only; two target Gray letters reuse explicit accepted primary reading. Three additional Watson records independently read with all bodies, enclosures, annotations, footnotes and bibliography. Original XML attributes, postal marks and Emma handwriting attribution checked. Raw HTML inspection confirms 1695 numerical corruption precedes extraction. Preserved and viewed 1743 diagram.
